h1.metric: correct next safe workflow gate on authored 30-case holdout
h1.interpretation: Jev was faster and cheaper than this GPT decision-only prompt and did not under-escalate authored critical cases; trivial rules were equally accurate with zero inference cost.

h5.metric: All four bounded next-step questions correct on 30-case holdout

matched_twelve_case_comparison.note: Exactly the same twelve preselected holdout cases, all travel + home types; no selection based on outcomes.

h5.interpretation: Batching reduced Jev latency and tokens versus four sequential Jev requests on the same twelve cases, but 2/12 bundled answers got an unnecessary evidence request wrong; no critical route under-escalation observed.

overall_estimate_scope.excluded: Previous six-case GPT extraction, A/B/C six-case study, earlier 20-case decisions and other experiments are not included.

hiring_summary: H1: Jev made 30/30 correct narrow workflow decisions versus 10/30 for this GPT prompt, but deterministic rules also got 30/30. H5: batching four Jev choices was roughly 3.3× faster in median latency than four serial Jev calls on the same 12 cases, but it produced two unnecessary evidence requests. Better speed, not identical quality.
limitations: New deterministic synthetic verified-fact records, not expert-labelled insurance claims; upstream source extraction and verification assumed and not measured.
One developer-authored generator with dev and holdout phrase variants; the benchmark is not real-world or independently evaluated.
GPT's poor gate performance is specific to this prompt/model/configuration, not general evidence GPT cannot classify or route.
The exact policy logic can be expressed as inexpensive deterministic Python; simple code matches or beats both models on this test.
H5 30-case full result and 12-case matched sequential result have different denominators; never compare their costs without matching the same 12 cases.
No human claims operation cost, actual provider invoice, payment authority or complete production workflow tested.
Output includes only allowed workflow gates. Continuing remaining checks is not a claims approval.
Provider API latency is not complete end-to-end handling time; no retries or production rate limits tested.
